page: Microsoft Azure D8a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DAv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs (4 physical cores with 2 threads per core) operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The CPU includes 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory (4.0 GB per core) and includes 205 GB of local SSD storage. No GPU is present.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average performance across most standard operations. The server achieves average ratings in Geekbench single-core (1561.0) and multi-core (6259.0) tests, as well as in Passmark CPU (11954.75) and memory (2604.54) metrics. However, stress-ng single-core CPU performance is poor (770.98, bottom 10%), and multi-core performance is weak (3078.76, bottom 25%). Large block memory write bandwidth is also weak at 24.77 GB/sec, though small block cached read bandwidth remains average at 514.53 GB/sec.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and bundled 205 GB local SSD, the D8a_v4 offers standard resource density for general-purpose workloads. It is suitable for tasks such as static web serving (9.56 GB/sec throughput), database operations, and light software compilation. It is not recommended for compute-intensive workloads that require high single-core performance or heavy multi-threaded decompression, where it shows performance bottlenecks.
description: The Microsoft Azure D8a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine from the DAv4 family, utilizing the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is configured with an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz, providing 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores. The hardware profile includes 32.0 GB of RAM (4.0 GB per core) and 205 GB of local SSD storage, with no GPU acceleration. Performance benchmarks show average capabilities for most tasks, including Geekbench multi-core execution, static web serving, and database operations, though single-core and multi-core stress-ng performance is relatively weak. This virtual machine is best suited for balanced general-purpose workloads, static web hosting, and standard database operations where extreme single-core compute performance is not a primary requirement.
